dedupe_keys.name: igs multi gnss experiment mgex data and products

description: The Multi-GNSS Experiment (MGEX) was set up by the IGS to track, collate and analyse all available GNSS signals, including BeiDou, Galileo, QZSS, NavIC, modernised GPS and GLONASS and any interesting satellite-based augmentation systems. Contents: a global data network of multi-GNSS stations, precise orbits and clocks, broadcast ephemerides, differential code biases, product descriptions, metadata in SINEX format, and analyses such as product availability, signal transmissions, clock time series and satellite laser ranging residuals. Producer: the IGS MGEX pilot project, chaired by Oliver Montenbruck, with analysis centres characterising new satellites and signals. Coverage: global, per constellation (GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou, QZSS, NavIC, SBAS). Access: pages for data, products and metadata on the IGS site; downloads sit in IGS data centres. Licence and cost: free; no licence text was read. Caveats: the page describes a pilot whose products and constellation coverage change as systems mature, and the page read does not list file names or latency. Simulation uses: it supplies open multi-constellation orbit, clock and signal data for availability and resilience models of positioning and timing services. It complements the IGS precise products record (data-igs-gnss-products).
